record.paper_title: Kirby diagrams, trisections and gems of PL 4-manifolds: relationships, results and open problems
record.original_question: Given a gem, can one automatically test whether the edge-ordering condition (*) of Proposition 11 holds and, when it does, algorithmically extract the specific bicolored cycles that determine a trisection diagram of the associated gem-induced trisection?

evidence.quote: Starting from a given gem, it is obviously possible to check in an automatic way whether condition (*) of Proposition 11 is satisfied; if so, it should not be difficult to detect algorithmically the bicolored cycles yielding a trisection diagram of the associated gem-induced trisection.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. A *gem* (graph-encoded manifold) of dimension 4 is a finite, regular, edge-5-colored multigraph $(\Gamma,\gamma)$ with color set $\Delta_4=\{0,1,2,3,4\}$ such that, for each $i\in\Delta_4$, the subgraph $\Gamma_{\hat i}$ obtained by deleting all edges of color $i$ encodes the boundary of a regular neighborhood of the vertex of color $i$ in the associated colored triangulation; equivalently, the dual ball-complex $K(\Gamma)$ is a closed PL 4-manifold $M^4$. For each unordered pair $\{i,j\}\subset\Delta_4$, a *bicolored cycle of colors $\{i,j\}$* is a connected component of the subgraph of $\Gamma$ induced by edges of colors $i$ and $j$; such a component is an even-length cycle alternating in colors $i$ and $j$.

A trisection of a closed orientable PL 4-manifold $M^4$ is a decomposition $M^4=X_1\cup X_2\cup X_3$ where each $X_h$ is a 4-dimensional 1-handlebody, the pairwise intersections $X_h\cap X_{h+1}$ are 3-dimensional handlebodies, and the triple intersection $\Sigma=X_1\cap X_2\cap X_3$ is a closed orientable surface; the trisection is described by a *trisection diagram* consisting of three cut systems of curves on $\Sigma$.

Suppose Proposition P below produces, from any gem $(\Gamma,\gamma)$ of a closed orientable PL 4-manifold satisfying a combinatorial condition (⋆) on the cyclic ordering of the five colors around each vertex, a *gem-induced trisection* of $M^4=K(\Gamma)$ whose central surface, handlebody decompositions, and cut systems are each realized by certain explicit families of bicolored cycles of $\Gamma$.

Problem. Design and prove correctness of an algorithm that, given as input a 5-edge-colored multigraph $(\Gamma,\gamma)$ representing a closed PL 4-manifold:

(a) decides in finite (and ideally polynomial) time whether the edge-ordering condition (⋆) of Proposition P is satisfied by $(\Gamma,\gamma)$; and

(b) when (⋆) holds, outputs the explicit lists of bicolored cycles of $(\Gamma,\gamma)$ that determine a trisection diagram $(\Sigma;\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$ of the gem-induced trisection of $M^4$.

Provide complexity bounds for both subroutines.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open algorithmic problem in recent surveys on gems and trisections of PL 4-manifolds (2025). Related work (e.g., "Estimating trisection genus via gem theory", arXiv:2504.04434, and "Trisections of PL 4-manifolds arising from colored triangulations", arXiv:2312.01902) develops the theoretical framework but does not provide a published, fully implemented algorithm with proven correctness for both detection of condition (⋆) and extraction of the bicolored-cycle data of the trisection diagram. No source confirming a complete solution was found.

status_evidence.title: Kirby diagrams, trisections and gems of PL 4-manifolds: relationships, results and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing open problems on gem-induced trisections, including the algorithmic detection of condition (*) and extraction of bicolored cycles giving a trisection diagram.
status_evidence.claim: The algorithmic question is explicitly listed among open problems.

status_evidence.title: Trisections of PL 4-manifolds arising from colored triangulations
status_evidence.snippet: Develops gem-induced trisections from colored triangulations satisfying combinatorial conditions on color orderings.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the theoretical proposition but not an implemented algorithm with complexity analysis.

status_evidence.title: Estimating trisection genus via gem theory
status_evidence.snippet: Uses gem theory to estimate trisection genus; does not give a general algorithm extracting bicolored-cycle trisection diagrams.
status_evidence.claim: Recent related work does not resolve the algorithmic problem.
